# January 14, 2027 - Shutdown of GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, mini - without required notice

On October 14, 2026, we notified developers using (the title’s) models of their deprecation and removal from the API on January 14, 2027.

There was no alternate notice such as described that I had seen. The only notice was the deprecation page saying that same language.

OpenAI writes:

We provide the following minimum notice periods before model retirement:

In the past before that declaration, OpenAI has even provided a year notice between deprecation and shutoff. [...] ### Related topics

| Topic |  | Replies | Views | Activity |
 ---  --- 
| What is the sunset date for gpt-4o-mini?  Deprecations | 4 | 2246 | January 14, 2026 |
| Deprecation date for gpt-4o-mini  API | 0 | 1800 | August 19, 2025 |
| Clarification needed: Is only gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07 deprecated, or the entire gpt-5-mini family?  Deprecations | 2 | 735 | October 6, 2026 |
| OpenAI is winding down the fine-tuning API and platform - Discussion Thread  Deprecations | 2 | 3559 | May 8, 2026 |
| Is GPT 4.1 Mini API getting retired? GPT 5 Mini too SLOW  API | 7 | 1986 | February 10, 2026 |

Powered by Discourse, best viewed with JavaScript enabled [...] These two model families, including the mini versions are extremely “generally available”, also having fine-tuning models that this also directly impacts - the end of any fine-tunings. The models certainly do not fall under “Specialized variants” for an exception.

I conclude that the shutoff must be pushed back to at least April 14.

# What is the sunset date for gpt-4o-mini?

I am seeking clarification on the final retirement date for the GPT-4o-mini (2024-07-18) snapshot. I have seen documentation indicating a sunset date of February 27, 2026.

Thanks for the clarification!

The complete list of deprecations can be found here.

There are currently no announced deprecations for `gpt-4o-mini`, what you are referring is probably related to a recent announcement of deprecation for `chatgpt-4o-latest`.

`gpt-4o-mini`
`chatgpt-4o-latest`

On November 18th, 2025, we notified developers using `chatgpt-4o-latest` model snapshot of its deprecation and removal from the API on February 17, 2026.

`chatgpt-4o-latest` [...] Thanks for that info. Very useful.

### Related topics

| Topic |  | Replies | Views | Activity |
 ---  --- 
| Deprecation date for gpt-4o-mini  API | 0 | 1744 | August 19, 2025 |
| Clarification needed: Is only gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07 deprecated, or the entire gpt-5-mini family?  Deprecations | 1 | 472 | June 16, 2026 |
| Any plans to deprecate the GPT-4 Turbo preview models?  API | 0 | 574 | May 8, 2024 |
| Deprecation dates for new 4o versions  Deprecations gpt-4o | 0 | 625 | September 17, 2024 |
| How long can i expect to be able to access a specific version of a model?  Deprecations gpt-4 | 1 | 264 | May 12, 2025 |

Powered by Discourse, best viewed with JavaScript enabled [...] We could use the general model name (instead of specific dated versions). However, we’d prefer to have a more repeatable system with specific dated models.

I had looked at the deprecations page but it doesn’t list specific dated model.

The moment that a model (or software feature) is given a lifespan, it would be deprecated.

Not appearing there means no immediate shutoff plans.

Although there is no formal pattern to guide your planning and maximum lifecycle, what can be observed is six months notice if there is a direct replacement, a year if there is no equivalent. Or as little as three months if it is a preview model or merely a test surface (like gpt-chat).

Thanks for that info. Very useful.

# Retiring GPT‑4o, GPT‑4.1, GPT‑4.1 mini, and OpenAI o4-mini in ChatGPT

Share

On February 13, 2026, alongside the previously announced retirement⁠ of GPT‑5 (Instant and Thinking), we will retire GPT‑4o, GPT‑4.1, GPT‑4.1 mini, and OpenAI o4-mini from ChatGPT. In the API, there are no changes at this time.

While this announcement applies to several older models, GPT‑4o deserves special context. [...] Changes like this take time to adjust to, and we’ll always be clear about what’s changing and when. We know that losing access to GPT‑4o will feel frustrating for some users, and we didn’t make this decision lightly. Retiring models is never easy, but it allows us to focus on improving the models most people use today.
